html:
Indo-Guyanese are the descendants of Indian indentured labourers brought to British Guiana from 1838 to 1917. The first two ships, the Whitby and the Hesperus, arrived on 5 May 1838, now Indian Arrival Day.

After the end of slavery, the freed Africans left the sugar estates for villages of their own, and planters looked to India for cheap labour. About 240,000 Indians came, bound by five-year contracts. Most stayed, and many later bought land and grew rice.

They became the largest group in Guyana, with their own Hindu and Muslim festivals, food and music. Politics came to divide largely between Indian and African Guyanese, as in the rivalry of Cheddi Jagan and Forbes Burnham. The same system of Indian indenture shaped Trinidad and Suriname.
